slot.brief: Simple percentage composition → empirical formula problem: given % of C, H and O (or just two elements + oxygen by difference), ask the empirical formula or the simplest whole-number ratio.

stem: An organic compound contains $54.5\%$ carbon, $9.1\%$ hydrogen and the rest oxygen. Its empirical formula is:

verdicts.working: Assume 100 g: C = 54.5/12, H = 9.1/1, O = 36.4/16 mol. Dividing by the smallest gives the ratio 2:4:1, so the empirical formula is C₂H₄O.
issues: The images for options A and C conflict with their listed formulas: A depicts propanal (C₃H₆O), and C depicts a ketone with formula C₄H₈O, not C₄H₈O₂.

working:
Assume $100~\text{g}$: $54.5~\text{g C} \Rightarrow 54.5/12 = 4.542\ \text{mol}$; $9.1~\text{g H} \Rightarrow 9.1/1 = 9.1\ \text{mol}$; Oxygen $=100-54.5-9.1=36.4\ \text{g} \Rightarrow 36.4/16=2.275\ \text{mol}$. Divide by $2.275$: C = $2.0$, H = $4.0$, O = $1.0$. Empirical formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$.

Independent check: Assume 100 g: C = 54.5/12, H = 9.1/1, O = 36.4/16 mol. Dividing by the smallest gives the ratio 2:4:1, so the empirical formula is C₂H₄O.
solution: Assume $100\,\text{g}$ of the compound. The mole amounts are $n_C=54.5/12$, $n_H=9.1/1$, and $n_O=36.4/16$.\n$$n_C:n_H:n_O=2.275:4.55:1.1375=2:4:1$$\nHence the empirical formula is $\mathrm{C_2H_4O}$.
